rationale: Structure is well organized with clear sections. Faithfulness suffers from fabricated formula 'Intelligence + Continual Learning = Expertise', an invented graph, and a wrong Anthropic statistic ($40B vs $40-60M). Coverage misses the bug-review example, many notable quotes, and two components of the continual-learning framework (world models, value estimation). Precision is low: all quote timestamps are incorrect (e.g., 635s vs 06:34), and quotes are not verbatim ('reusable structure' vs 'reusable structures'; expertise quote mixed with definition). Compression is moderate: definitions and points are repeated across overview, topic_map, and compressed sections.
hallucinations: Anthropic's annualized run rate grew 400 times to $40 billion in under two years.
Graph of Expertise vs. Raw Intelligence showing strong continual learning achieving exponential escape expertise.
Different continual learning algorithms set the slope of the learning curve relative to raw intelligence.
MIT report showing 95% of generative AI pilots at companies failing due to brittle errors in enterprise settings.
Expertise is accumulated and situated competence: the ability to act reliably, efficiently, and with judgment to achieve reproducibly superior performance in a particular domain.
Continual learning is adaptive compression of experience into reusable structure for future behavior.
